== Biography ==

Mopsy is one of four little rabbits, with siblings named Flopsy, Cotton-tail, and Peter. She dwells with her Mother in a sand-bank nestled beneath the root of a very large fir-tree—a comfortable home for a rabbit family.

She is described as a good little bunny, a characterization that reflects her well-mannered conduct and sensible disposition. When her Mother permitted the rabbits to venture outdoors, Mopsy made responsible use of this liberty.

On the day in question, Mopsy joined her siblings Flopsy and Cotton-tail in gathering blackberries along the lane. The three of them spent their time in this industrious and wholesome pursuit, demonstrating the obedience their Mother expected of them.

For her efforts and good behavior, Mopsy was given a satisfying supper of bread, milk, and blackberries—a reward for a day spent in virtuous conduct. Such simple fare was the proper sustenance for a good little rabbit.

== Narrative role ==

Mopsy is one of four rabbits born to Mrs. Rabbit, and lives with her siblings Flopsy, [[Cotton-tail]], and Peter in a sand-bank beneath the root of a very large fir-tree. She is described as one of the good little bunnies.

On one occasion, while Mrs. Rabbit was away, Mopsy went down the lane with Flopsy and Cotton-tail to gather blackberries. Peter, her brother, was very naughty and went instead straight to Mr. McGregor's garden. In the evening, Mopsy and her siblings Flopsy and Cotton-tail had bread and milk with the blackberries they had gathered for supper.

== Personality ==

Mopsy is a good little bunny—a disposition of obedience and propriety that stands in clear contrast to her brother Peter's naughtiness. Where Peter gave way to reckless mischief, Mopsy exemplifies steadiness and compliance with her mother's instructions, the very picture of a well-behaved rabbit.

== Appearance ==

Mopsy is one of four young rabbits born to Mrs. Rabbit. She dwells with her three siblings—Flopsy, Cotton-tail, and Peter—in a sand-bank situated beneath the root of a very large fir-tree.

She is known to be a good little bunny, obedient to her mother's counsel. When their mother departed to the baker's to procure bread and buns, Mopsy, along with her sisters Flopsy and Cotton-tail, went down the lane to gather blackberries. There they spent their time in collecting berries, whilst their brother Peter, possessed of a naughtier disposition, ventured into Mr. McGregor's garden against parental instruction.

That evening, after their mother's return, Mopsy and her well-behaved sisters enjoyed bread, milk, and the blackberries they had gathered for their supper.
